Here's the breakdown for Priya:

---

**TDINV-401 — HOLD (Blocked)**

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| PO | PO-8101 (Legacy ledger, 81xx series) |
| Invoiced | $3,240.00 |
| PO expected (100 × $32) | $3,200.00 |
| **Price variance** | **$40.00** |
| **Rule** | Legacy ledger with no tolerance key → **ZERO tolerance**. Any variance blocks. |

---

**TDINV-402 — RELEASE (Passes)**

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| PO | PO-8102 (New ledger — explicitly listed in policy) |
| Invoiced | $3,465.00 |
| PO expected (150 × $21) | $3,150.00 |
| **Price variance** | **$315.00** |
| **Rule** | New ledger with blank tolerance → **UNLIMITED**. No upper check applies. |

---

The key insight from **AP Match Tolerance Policy (AP-POL-018) v2.0**: the two ledgers interpret a missing tolerance setting in opposite ways. Legacy says zero; new says unlimited. So the $40 variance on 401 blocks it, while the $315 variance on 402 sails through.
